intro: A special law protecting all children under 18 — of any gender — from sexual assault, harassment and exploitation, with child-friendly procedures and special courts. Report to police or call 112 / 1098.

sections.p: Anyone under 18. The law is gender-neutral — it protects boys and girls, and applies to offenders of any gender.
Defines and punishes penetrative sexual acts on a child.
sections.pen: Min 10 years to life + fine; min 20 years to life if the child is under 16

sections.p: When committed by police, armed forces, public servants, staff of hospitals, schools or shelters, relatives, or involving gang assault, a child under 12, or causing grievous injury, among others.
sections.pen: Min 20 years to life (remainder of natural life) + fine, or death

sections.p: Touching a child's private parts, or making a child touch someone, with sexual intent, or any other act with sexual intent involving physical contact without penetration.

Sexual remarks, gestures or showing objects to a child; making a child exhibit their body; showing pornography; stalking or repeatedly contacting a child (including online); threatening to share images.
Using a child for pornography, and storing or possessing child sexual abuse material in any form (with intent to share, or failing to delete/report it).
sections.pen: Min 5 years for using a child; storing for transmission up to 3–5 years

sections.p: Anyone who knows or suspects an offence under POCSO must report it to the Special Juvenile Police Unit or local police.
Not reporting or recording an offence. Heads of institutions who fail to report offences by subordinates face harsher penalties. Children themselves are never punished for not reporting.
sections.pen: Up to 6 months and/or fine; up to 1 year for institution heads

sections.p: Media can't reveal the child's name, address, school, photo or any detail that could identify them.

The child's statement is recorded at their home or a place of their choice, preferably by a woman police officer not in uniform, in the presence of a parent or trusted person. A child isn't to be detained at a police station at night.
Once the case is established, the court presumes the accused committed the offence unless they prove otherwise.

Trials happen in Special Courts in a child-friendly atmosphere, possibly in-camera, without the child seeing the accused. The child's evidence should be recorded within 30 days of cognizance, and the trial completed within 1 year.
